messages.subject: What can cause the estimate for Em to be NA?
messages.subject_clean: What can cause the estimate for Em to be NA?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Murray
When using Enrm, please can you clarify what can cause the estimate for Em to be NA. Initially I thought it was due to there being no spatial recaptures but I have seen that sometimes I get NA for Em but a number bigger than 1 for En2.

I have read the caveat in the vignette about Em for count detectors but don't think this is the issue here. As a second question related to the caveat, with one occasion and no actual times of capture does the calculation treat the order of captures as consecutive in time for that individual?

Many thanks

Greg

messages.subject: Re: What can cause the estimate for Em to be NA?
messages.subject_clean: What can cause the estimate for Em to be NA?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Greg
I haven't come across that, and it's a long time since I wrangled those formulae. Eyeballing the C code where I think the problem must lie: I'm guessing you have an isolated detector or isolated mask point that generates a zero in a denominator... That's a long shot. Can you provide an example I can use for debugging? On the second question, no I don't think the calculation treats 'captures' as consecutive in time. It just uses the unpublished approximate formulae as shown.
Murray

Hi
At the moment I am trying to generate Enrm summaries for a grid design in a particular study area. Here are the Enrm results, you can see the NaN for Em and the En2 of 3.6. I attach the mask and trap file used here. Note that I would expect some recaptures as I am using spacing of 1 sigma.

scenF <- make.scenarios (trapsindex = 1, detectfn = 'HHN', D = 0.00015, lambda0 = 5, sigma = 2000, noccasions = 1)
nrm.scenF.gridsF <- scenarioSummary(scenF, traps = grid.F, mask = CLTsimp.nobuff)

> nrm.scenF.gridsF
  scenario trapsindex noccasions nrepeats       D lambda0 sigma detectfn    En     Er
1        1          1          1        1 0.00015       5  2000       14 4.211 61.045
   Em   En2      esa CF rotRSE rotRSEB arrayN arrayspace arrayspan saturation
1 NaN 3.618 28073.35  1 0.4873  0.4616     40          1    8.2462  0.7943793

Thanks!

Greg

messages.subject: Re: What can cause the estimate for Em to be NA?
messages.subject_clean: What can cause the estimate for Em to be NA?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the concrete example. There was a numerical issue (divide-by-zero in C++ code when squared hazard became very small). I'm tempted to blame that on your fairly extreme design (detectors clustered in corner of large area) but really it shouldn't have happened. I saw the problem coming in the original code, but didn't catch it properly.

The working version of secrdesign on GitHub is now fixed, and you can access a Windows binary here <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/secrdesign_2.9.0.zip> and the source secrdesign_2.9.0.tar.gz here <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/secrdesign_2.9.0.tar.gz>. I would still advise a few simulations to check the E(m) are reasonable.

Murray

messages.subject: Can I combine CL and FL methods?
messages.subject_clean: Can I combine CL and FL methods?
messages.body_plain:
Hello group,
I'd like to model density for my project (with several possible covariates), but also have several plausible combinations of detection sub-models.

Would it be logical (or rather, not mathematically correct) to use CL = true to narrow the top-ranked detection submodel combos, which will then be plonked into a CL = false density model ?

My thought process is: speed up the models by using CL /narrowing down possible FL models rather than testing many plausible combos. Bit of best of both worlds? OR does this mashup fall under the same rule as "don't compare AIC between CL and FL models?"

Appreciate all feedback and direction,
Thanks
Sam

messages.subject: Re: Can I combine CL and FL methods?
messages.subject_clean: Can I combine CL and FL methods?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Sam, and welcome to the group.
Maximizing the conditional likelihood produces identical estimates of detection parameters to those from maximizing the full likelihood (apart from negligible numerical effects) if the default distribution is used for n (Poisson rather than binomial). So It seems perfectly reasonable to use CL to home in on a good detection model. Of course you cannot subsequently compare CL and full models by AIC. With secr.fit(..., details = list(distribution = "binomial")) then there may be some daylight between CL and full approaches, but very little in my experience.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: How to specify occasion per session
messages.subject_clean: How to specify occasion per session
messages.body_plain:
By default make.capthist() and read.capthist() assume that the final occasion (and hence the number of occasions) is the largest occasion in your capture dataset. However, both functions have argument 'noccasions' that may be used to specify the number of occasions, with exactly your situation in mind. For multi-session data the noccasions argument can be a vector with one number per session.
